introHeading: Wedding photo booths for Queens-sized guest lists
introParas: Queens weddings tend to run bigger than anywhere else we work — multigenerational catering hall receptions in Astoria and Flushing that seat two hundred, and Long Island City loft weddings with the ceiling height to match. A booth that works fine for a hundred-guest reception starts to bottleneck fast at that scale, so we plan Queens bookings around throughput from the start rather than treating every wedding the same size.

The mirror booth is still the right base choice for most Queens receptions — the full-length format handles a whole wedding party and works for guests from the flower girl to the grandparents, which matters at the family-heavy guest lists common in Forest Hills and Jamaica. Where it gets interesting is past roughly 150 guests: at that point we routinely pair the mirror booth with a roaming attendant so the seated tables at your Astoria or Flushing catering hall get covered directly instead of everyone funneling into one line all night. For a younger Ridgewood or Long Island City crowd who will post the clip before the band's second set, the 360 booth tends to see the heaviest use.

On logistics: we carry a $3 million policy and turn a certificate of insurance around the same day you give us your venue's contact — standard for the catering halls that dominate Queens wedding venues. We arrive an hour ahead and set up in about 20 minutes, in a 10ft x 10ft footprint where the room allows it or 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance where it's tighter, plus a standard outlet within 15 feet that isn't shared with the DJ. Queens is a standard service area with no surprise travel fee — we quote it from your venue's ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Wedding Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: How many hours should we book for a Queens wedding?
faqs.a: Three to four hours covers most receptions, though larger Astoria and Flushing catering hall weddings sometimes run longer. Send us your guest count and run sheet and we'll suggest a start time and whether a second attendant makes sense before we quote you extra hours.

faqs.q: Our guest list is large — can one booth keep up?
faqs.a: Past about 150 guests, which is common at Queens catering halls, we usually suggest pairing your static booth with a roaming attendant. That way seated tables get covered directly instead of everyone lining up at one station all night.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee in Queens?
faqs.a: No surprise fees. Queens is a standard service area and we quote any travel cost from your venue's ZIP code before you book — Long Island City, Astoria, Flushing, Forest Hills, Jamaica and Ridgewood are all regular territory for us.

faqs.q: Which booth works best for a Queens wedding?
faqs.a: The mirror booth is the safest choice for the family-heavy, multigenerational guest lists common at Queens receptions. For a younger Long Island City or Ridgewood crowd, the 360 booth gets used the hardest.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: Optimal is a 10ft x 10ft footprint, with 8ft x 8ft and 7.5ft of ceiling clearance as the minimum — usually not an issue in Queens's larger catering halls, but worth checking if your venue is a smaller loft space. We also need a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet, not shared with the DJ.

About 20 minutes once we're in the room. We build in a full hour ahead of your scheduled start so everything is tested before your first guest walks in. If you need us on site earlier than that, idle time is $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Can you send our venue a certificate of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us your venue's contact — standard practice for the catering halls most Queens weddings are held at.

faqs.q: Do we get every photo from the night, not just the prints?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image lands in an online gallery you can download in full and share with guests, on top of the unlimited prints handed out on the night.
